scope_note: This delivery covers §3.1 (single durable write authority), part of §3.2 (frozen capability contract, the net-new update_metadata_cas capability, correct action-owner semantics for the BFF Strategy adapter), and part of §3.3 (CAS + atomic idempotent receipt, initial auth enforcement on the new metadata route). Those remaining gaps are recorded explicitly in services/registry/first_release_contract.json (retirement.remaining_scope_not_owned_by_this_task) rather than silently treated as complete; architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §4 explicitly permits Registry to merge before all consumers once its own required checks pass.

summary: PostgresRegistryStore (pg_store.py): durable RegistryEntry owner store using services/foundation/postgres_json_store.py's PostgresJsonOwnerStore. CAS-guarded update() binds the caller's base snapshot (not a fetch-immediately-before-write); commit_metadata_cas() commits an entry mutation and its idempotent command receipt in one Postgres transaction via a new PostgresJsonOwnerStore.transaction()/conn= extension.

Fixed a latent concurrent-first-bootstrap race in postgres_json_store.ensure_postgres_schema/PostgresJsonOwnerStore.bootstrap (23505 unique-violation when two owner-store instances race their first CREATE SCHEMA/TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) — proven with a dedicated concurrency test against a real database, affects every consumer of this shared primitive.

storage.py: build_registry_store()/get_store() select memory (test double, unchanged default for existing tests) vs postgres (REGISTRY_STORE_BACKEND=postgres, fails closed on missing DSN rather than silently downgrading) — mirrors services/governance/pg_store.py's build_approval_decision_store pattern. Fixed a pre-existing aliasing bug: RegistryStore.get()/list_by_strategy() returned live references into the store's internal dict, so a caller mutating the returned object silently mutated durable state outside of update(); both now return copies, matching real backend semantics.

split_api.py: advance_artifact_state() and update_deployment_summary() now pass a base snapshot to store.update()/store.update_deployment_summary() and translate a stale-snapshot conflict into RegistryConflictError (HTTP 409) instead of an unconditional overwrite. Added update_metadata() — the net-new 'allowed metadata update with CAS' capability required by architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §3.2, including a command_key idempotent-replay path.

service.py: new PATCH /api/registry/entries/{registry_id}/metadata route; verified-caller auth enforcement (services/runtime_auth_inbound.validate_request_auth) wired onto this one net-new route via _authenticate_registry_write (PANTHEON_REGISTRY_AUTH_MODE, default permissive at the library level, hardened to strict in docker-compose.yml/control.yml per §3.3's 'no anonymous compatibility path').

command_contract.py: canonical STRATEGY_ACTIONS matrix. update_params resolves to Registry's update_metadata_cas capability; submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive resolve to governance_review/promotion/runtime and carry no Registry capability, so a caller can no longer relabel one business action as another.

BFF strategy_adapter.py: _execute_strategy_action no longer fabricates a resulting_status from a static action->status map. update_params now performs a real GET (base metadata) + PATCH (CAS) + GET (verified readback) sequence against the Registry owner; submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive raise ActionUnavailableError naming the exact non-Registry owner instead of returning an inferred success. RankingFormula/Ranking handling in the same file is untouched (architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §3.2 explicitly preserves that unrelated scope).

BFF base.py: fixed http_request_json's method dispatch, which previously routed any non-GET call (including the new PATCH) through command_executor._post_json, which hardcodes method='POST' — silently sending the wrong HTTP verb. Added registry_url() helper.

No parallel full-spec/revision authority or duplicate route exists in the currently mounted app (confirmed by enumerating all 23 mounted routes); the retirement inventory in first_release_contract.json documents this explicitly rather than claiming a retirement that was never needed.

Front-loaded shared HTTP slice (formal artifact-contract revision 2026-09-06T03:31:41Z, after PR #5620's draft head remained unaccepted): added real-socket regressions in test_strategy_registry_owner_prerequisite.py::TestHttpRequestJsonMethodDispatch proving base.py's http_request_json actually sends GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE as the requested verb (not silently coerced to POST — the exact bug this task already fixed in base.py, which also affected capital_adapter.py's pre-existing PATCH calls), forwards Authorization/X-MFA-Token headers, propagates a real 409/5xx owner error, and honors an explicit timeout instead of hanging. Discovered and fixed a second instance of the same class of bug while writing these regressions: command_executor.py's _get_json/_post_json (used by every other domain adapter through the same http_request_json entrypoint) unconditionally re-wrapped an already-'Bearer '-prefixed auth_token into 'Bearer Bearer ...', unlike base.py's own fallback path, which already guarded against this — command_executor.py now uses the same not-already-prefixed guard for both.
